5a-E1.name: Refund returns REFUND_PENDING
5a-E1.description: POST /api/payments/refund returns the Refund in REFUND_PENDING status (refund initiated, not yet confirmed)

5a-E2.name: Payment state consistent (atomic writes)
5a-E2.description: Refund record + reversal Dr/Cr LedgerEntry pair + PAYMENT_REFUND_PENDING AuditLog + PAYMENT_REFUND_REQUESTED Outbox event + IdempotencyKey all commit in SAME txn

5a-E3.name: Idempotency preserved (same key → same Refund)
5a-E3.description: Same Idempotency-Key returns the SAME Refund — no duplicate Refund, no duplicate reversal entries

5a-E4.name: Concurrent refund requests → exactly 1 Refund
5a-E4.description: Two simultaneous POSTs with the same Idempotency-Key produce exactly 1 Refund (one wins, other cached)

5a-E5.name: Publisher retry → no duplicate refund
5a-E5.description: Publisher retry does NOT duplicate the external refund — idempotency check (Refund.status === REFUNDED) prevents second refund call

invariant.description: Refund flow (P0-04) mirrors the Wave-4 4c capture pattern: refund route writes Refund + reversal Dr/Cr + AuditLog + Outbox event inside ONE txn (atomic); publisher calls refundRazorpayPayment() OUTSIDE any txn (TRANSACTION_RETRY_INVARIANT preserved); idempotency check (Refund.status === REFUNDED) prevents duplicate external refund on retry.

governance.note: Wave-5 Sub-Wave 5a evidence: P0-04 refund flow verified on staging PostgreSQL. realPayments=false (demo mode — refundRazorpayPayment returns mock success). No production traffic touched. Test data cleaned up.
